name: AXIN2-related polyposis

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic germline mutation in the AXIN2 gene
Detection of multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps (typically >10) on colonoscopy
Family history of colorectal cancer or polyposis consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Presence of ectodermal dysplasia features such as hypodontia or missing permanent teeth

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic AXIN2 mutation plus multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; ectodermal dysplasia features support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

laboratory: Mild iron deficiency anemia due to chronic bleeding
Normal routine blood tests unless malignancy present
imaging: CT or MRI for detection of desmoid tumors or extra-colonic masses
other: Dental examination showing hypodontia or other ectodermal dysplasia features

distinguishingFeatures: APC gene mutations instead of AXIN2
Typically hundreds to thousands of polyps
More frequent desmoid tumors and osteomas
Mutations in mismatch repair genes (e.g., MLH1, MSH2)
Higher risk of extracolonic cancers such as endometrial carcinoma

redFlags: Multiple colorectal adenomatous polyps detected on colonoscopy
Family history of colorectal cancer or polyposis with ectodermal dysplasia features
references: Lejeune S et al. AXIN2 mutations cause familial tooth agenesis and predispose to colorectal cancer. Am J Hum Genet. 2006.
Ngeow J, Eng C. AXIN2-related colorectal polyposis and cancer predisposition. Clin Genet. 2015.
